title: Cyclone Warning: The Long Swell
intro_lines: The horizon bruises purple.
Swells march in slow, heavy lines.
Tide-Puck's frill lies flat. He growls at the receding surf.

choices.label: Grant shelter; earn a blade

outcomes.text: He shares UTC patrol routes. You brace the outpost before the eye hits.
He steals a cutlass in the night. Tide-Puck wakes you; the thief flees empty-handed.
He's a UTC plant. He signals a patrol before vanishing. The storm masks their approach.

choices.label: Turn him away; seal the walls

outcomes.text: You reinforce the palisade. The deserter curses you into the wind.
He returns with a UTC boarding party at the storm's height. You fight in wind and rain.

choices.label: Flee to the sea caves with Tide-Puck

outcomes.text: Tide-Puck guides you through a submerged tunnel. The camp weathers the worst alone.
The tunnel floods. You claw through an air pocket, losing gear but surviving.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk read weather signs from swell patterns and bird behaviour to survive four years on Juan Fernández; Tide-Puck's frill-flattening mirrors frigatebirds sensing pressure drops before cyclones (RMG).

title: Cyclone Landfall: The Eye's Silence
intro_lines: Wind screams like a gutted hull.
Palm trunks snap.
The eye passes overhead — unnatural quiet.

choices.label: Rally sailors to shore the walls

outcomes.text: The palisade holds. The back-wind tears the roof off the storehouse but the powder stays dry.
A flying spar crushes the cookfire. Burns spread to the fibre stores. You bucket seawater in the lull.

choices.label: Send Tide-Puck to scout the UTC wreck

outcomes.text: He returns with a waterlogged crate: UTC charts showing Tideborn ruin locations. Salt-ruined but legible.
He finds a live dark-binding crystal pulsing in the wreck. It screams in your mind. You bury it deep.
The back-wind catches him. He rides a gust back, wing torn. You stitch the membrane with sailcloth and catgut.

choices.label: Ride out the eyewall in the cellar

outcomes.text: The stone walls hold. You emerge to shattered jungle and a sea littered with UTC timber.
Storm surge floods the cellar. You swim for the hatch, dragging an unconscious sailor. He dies of swallowed seawater.

history_note: The 1761 L'Utile survivors on Tromelin kept one fire alive for fifteen years through cyclones, building 1.5 m thick coral walls with backs to the trade wind after a storm destroyed their first shelter (INRAP).

title: Cyclone Landfall: The Betrayal
intro_lines: The deserter's whistle cuts the gale.
UTC marines emerge from the jungle.
They knew your wall's weak face.

choices.label: Fight a retreating action to the cliffs

outcomes.text: You hold the ridge. Lightning silhouettes the UTC officer; a sniper's ball takes him. The patrol breaks.
The mud sucks boots off. A marine grapples you; Tide-Puck tears his throat. You limp away, leaving the camp burning.

choices.label: Surrender the relic shards; buy lives

outcomes.text: The officer takes the shards and your swords. 'Company business.' They leave you alive, camp intact.
The crystals shrieked when he touched them. The leviathan's rage hits the patrol. You flee in the chaos.

choices.label: Trigger the powder cache; collapse

outcomes.text: The blast seals the pass. UTC screams echo. The camp survives but the jungle path is gone for months.
Damp powder fizzes. The officer laughs. You're captured, marched to a UTC brig in irons.

history_note: Bartholomew Roberts' articles mandated death or marooning for desertion; UTC deserters historically faced impressment or execution, making betrayal a rational survival choice (Johnson 1724).

title: Lightning Fire: The Dry Thunder
intro_lines: Lightning stabs the ridge.
No rain follows — just the smell of ozone and scorched
A banyan crown erupts.

choices.label: Bucket chain from the well

outcomes.text: The line passes shells and helmets. You save the storehouse and the sail loft. Hands blister.
The well runs dry. The fire takes the quartermaster's hut. His charts burn; he weeps into rum.

choices.label: Cut a firebreak with axes and fire

outcomes.text: You fell a green belt. The backfire meets the main front. The camp survives in a blackened clearing.
Wind shifts. The backfire jumps the break. You lose the boat shed and a half-careened hull.

choices.label: Tide-Puck smothers embers with wet wings

outcomes.text: He dives through smoke, dousing hotspots. His wing-tips singe. You treat burns with aloe and shark oil.
A beam collapses. He shields a sailor, taking the weight. Ribs cracked. Weeks of recovery.
He herds the flock of terns nesting in the rafters. Their panicked flight spreads fire to the jungle canopy.

history_note: Tromelin castaways kept a single fire alive for fifteen years using wreck timber, driftwood, and the island's only shrub; lightning strikes on dry jungle were a constant threat they managed with communal vigilance (Archaeology Mag 2014).

title: King Tide: The Sea Takes Its Due
intro_lines: The moon hangs fat and low.
Water climbs the beach markers Silas carved.
The tide laps the palisade logs.

choices.label: Sandbag the well and storehouse

outcomes.text: The bags hold. The well stays sweet. You lose the beach drying racks but save the salt pork.
A wave bursts the barrier. Salt poisons the well. You'll need a solar still or rain catchment.

choices.label: Move critical stores to the sea cave

outcomes.text: Tide-Puck guides the line through the tidal tunnel. Powder, charts, and rum reach the high ledge dry.
The surge traps two sailors in the tunnel. You haul them out blue-lipped. The powder kegs stay below.

choices.label: Harvest the stranded reef life

outcomes.text: Tide pools yield octopus, sea cucumbers, and a trapped reef shark. Feast tonight; smoke the rest.
A stonefish spines your hand. Hot water helps but the limb swells. Three days of fever.
UTC scavengers on the reef claim the best pools. A musket ball kicks sand at your feet. You withdraw.

history_note: In the heat and rain, Pedro Serrano's provisions spoiled within two months; meat had to be dried in the sun to last.

title: Heatwave: The Doldrums' Fever
intro_lines: The air thickens to syrup.
No wind for six days.
Pitch bubbles from the careened hull's seams.

choices.label: Rig awnings and enforce siesta

outcomes.text: Canvas shades the camp. You ration water, wake only at dawn and dusk. No heat deaths this cycle.
The quartermaster hoards rum rations. A knife fight in the shade leaves two men bleeding. You maroon the instigator.

choices.label: Dig a communal solar still

outcomes.text: The still yields three gallons daily. Men line up with cups. Morale lifts; the cave stays cool.
The plastic sheeting fails. The pit collapses. You waste days and precious sailcloth for a cup of brackish water.

choices.label: Hunt nocturnal; sleep by day

outcomes.text: Tide-Puck flushes fruit bats and land crabs by torchlight. The cave stays cool. You gain weight.
A feral boar charges the torch-bearer. Tusks rip a thigh. You cauterize with a heated cutlass.
Sea kraits swarm the warm cave mouth. You seal the entrance with boulders, losing the cool air.

history_note: Careening meant beaching a ship at high tide, heeling it over and scraping off weed and teredo worm, leaving the crew exposed.

title: Sea Fog: The Grey Wolf
intro_lines: Fog rolls in on a breathless tide.
The reef vanishes.
Gulls fall silent. The horizon dissolves. Oars muffled.

choices.label: Light signal fires; hold position

outcomes.text: Three fires in a triangle. A free pirate cutter ghosts past, hails you. Trade news for rum and charts.
The fires draw a UTC patrol. They board silently. You hide relic shards in a false-bottomed chest.

choices.label: Send Tide-Puck to sniff the vessel

outcomes.text: He returns smelling of tar, sweat, and coconut oil — free pirates. They leave a barrel of salt beef.
He smells ozone and copper — dark-binding crystals. A UTC hunter-killer. You sink your longboat to hide it.
He doesn't return. Hours later a Tideborn scout finds him tangled in a ghost net. She cuts him free.

choices.label: Row silent reconnaissance with muffled

outcomes.text: You glide alongside a careened UTC frigate. Count guns, note crystal crates. Intel worth gold in Nassau.
A sentry coughs. You freeze. The fog lifts enough for a musket volley. One oarsman dies. You row for your life.
You drift into a Tideborn ruin's shadow. Ancient arches loom. A scout presses a pearl into your palm — a warning.

history_note: Pedro Serrano's smoke signals were ignored by ships fearing Serrana Bank's shoals; effective signalling required three fires in a triangle and green leaves for white smoke to distinguish distress from wreckers' false lights (Frontiers 2019).

title: Doldrums: The Painted Ship
intro_lines: Fourteen days without a breath.
The sea mirrors the sky.
Hull fouls with weed; teredo worms feast. Water runs low.

choices.label: Careen now; scrape the hull at high tide

outcomes.text: The keel bites sand. You plug wormholes, coat with tar and turtle fat. Speed returns. The shark circles closer.
The tide drops fast. The hull lists, cracking a rib. You jury-rig shores. Weeks of repair ahead.

choices.label: Distill seawater in the ship's coppers

outcomes.text: The coppers yield twenty gallons daily. You ration fairly. The shark gets nothing but bilge.
Salt scale clogs the condenser. A sailor drinks from the header — brine burns his throat. He dies screaming.

choices.label: Tide-Puck dives for bottom fish

outcomes.text: He drives grouper and snapper into the nets. Fresh meat and moisture. The crew cheers his name.
He brings a massive barracuda. You know the risk — ciguatera — but hunger wins. Three men twitch for days.
He surfaces with a Tideborn relic in his jaws — a coral key. The shark bumps the boat. Tide-Puck chatters defiance.

history_note: Golden Age pirates careened on sloping beaches at high tide, scraping teredo worm trails and coating hulls with tar, tallow, and turtle fat; crews were defenceless during careening, often landing guns as a beach battery (JMU thesis).

title: Waterspout: The Rope from Heaven
intro_lines: A finger of cloud descends, spinning.
The sea boils around its base.
It walks the reef toward you.

choices.label: Anchor in the lee of the cliff; ride it

outcomes.text: The spout passes two cables away. Spray strips paint. Your anchor holds. The cutter is gone.
The wind shifts. The spout lifts your stern. You cut the anchor cable, drifting into the reef. Hull breached.

choices.label: Row perpendicular to its path; outrun

outcomes.text: You pull for your lives. The spout's fringe tears a sail. You clear its path as it dissolves into rain.
A rogue wave capsizes the boat. You cling to the keel. Tide-Puck tows the unconscious to shore.

choices.label: Fire the swivel gun into the vortex

outcomes.text: The grapeshot disrupts the spin. The spout unravels, dropping a ton of seawater on the reef. You survive.
The shot passes through harmlessly. The spout veers toward the flash. You abandon ship for the jungle.
The concussion triggers a dark-binding crystal in the cutter's wreck. The spout hums purple. The leviathan wakes.

history_note: Waterspouts are documented hazards in tropical waters; 18th-century mariners fired cannon into them hoping to disrupt the vortex, a tactic mentioned in Royal Navy logs but of dubious effectiveness (NOAA reef hazards).

title: Rainy Season: The Green Rot
intro_lines: Thirty days of rain.
Moss thickens on ropes.
Mushrooms bloom in the powder kegs. Another coughs blood.

choices.label: Burn sulphur and herbs; fumigate

outcomes.text: The smoke drives mould from the stores. You lose some flavour but save the powder and sailcloth.
The fumes choke a sleeping sailor. He wakes gasping, lungs scarred. The surgeon bleeds him; he weakens.

choices.label: Build raised platforms; move stores off

outcomes.text: Pallet floors and beam shelves. Air circulates. The rot halts. You gain a second storey for the quartermaster.
Green timber warps in the damp. A shelf collapses, crushing the rum casks. The crew mourns the loss.

choices.label: Tide-Puck seeks the cave's dry chimney

outcomes.text: He finds a fissure where wind blows constant and dry. You move the powder and charts there. Safe at last.
The chimney houses a colony of oilbirds. Their guano burns the powder bags. You salvage half, cursing.
He leads you to a Tideborn shrine, dry and ancient. A stone tablet depicts the leviathan. You copy the glyphs.

history_note: Tromelin castaways battled mould and rot for fifteen years; they stored water in salvaged lead basins and built thick coral walls to manage damp, while the island's single shrub provided minimal dry fuel (Int J Osteoarchaeol 2021).

title: The Fog's Gift: Tideborn Warning
intro_lines: The Tideborn scout's pearl hums faint in your palm.
She spoke three words before vanishing: 'Crystal wakes
Dawn burns the fog.

choices.label: Sabotage the array before it charges

outcomes.text: You shatter the focusing crystals. The array screams, a sound like tearing metal. UTC patrol boats turn back.
The feedback loop detonates. A wave of pressure flattens the reef. You wake on the beach, ears bleeding.

choices.label: Steal the power core; bring it to Silas

outcomes.text: Tide-Puck retrieves the core — a living geode. Silas weeps; it's a Tideborn heart-stone. He knows the binding songs.
UTC divers cut the line. The core sinks. A patrol surrounds you. You trade the map fragment for your lives.

choices.label: Leave it; the leviathan is not your war

outcomes.text: You withdraw. The array charges. Weeks later, a tidal wave scours the UTC haven on the next isle. Survivors wash ashore.
The wave hits your isle too. The camp floods. Silas's charts are lost. You rebuild from memory and salt.

history_note: The 1761 Tromelin survivors built a boat from wreckage in two months and sailed for help, leaving sixty Malagasy slaves behind; fifteen years passed before rescue, during which they maintained fire, dug wells, and endured cyclones (Archaeology Mag 2014).
